source_text: Ἡ δὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἄγαν ὁρμῆς μὴ λογιζομένη, ὡς ἄνθρωπον, σπαράσσει τὸν χάρτην, κἀκεῖ δείκνυσι τὸ μισάνθρωπον. Οὕτω καὶ ὁ διάβολος ἐν τῇ εἰκόνι τὸ μισόθεον ἔδειξεν, ἐπειδὴ Θεοῦ προσάψασθαι οὐκ ἐδύνατο. Οὕτως ὁ εἰς ἡμᾶς πόλεμος ἀπόδειξιν ἔχει τοῦ θεομάχον εἶναι τὸν πονηρὸν, καὶ πρῶτον πολεμεῖν τῷ Δεσπότῃ. Ἐκεῖνος κατήγαγεν ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἱεριχὼ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀπὸ τῶν ὑψηλῶν ἐπὶ τὰ κοῖλα. Ἐπὶ μὲν τῆς ὀρεινῆς ἡ Ἱερουσαλήμ· ἡ δὲ Ἱεριχὼ κάτω ἐν τῇ ἁλμυρᾷ θαλάσσῃ. Εἴ τις ὑμῶν οἶδε τὸν τόπον, οἶδε τῶν λεγομένων τὴν ἀλήθειαν, ὅτι Ἱεριχὼ μὲν ἔχει τὰ κοῖλα τῆς Παλαιστίνης, Ἱερουσαλὴμ δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς κορυφῆς ἐρήρεισται, τὴν ἄκραν κατέχουσα τοῦ ὄρους τοῦ διὰ πάσης ἐκείνης τῆς χώρας ἀνεστηκότος . Ἀπὸ τοίνυν τῶν ὑψηλῶν ἐπὶ τὰ κάτω ἦλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἵνα τοῖς λῃσταῖς περιπέσῃ· τῆς ἀσφαλείας ἐξελθὼν τῆς κατὰ Ἱερου-σαλὴμ, ἵνα εὐάλωτος γένηται τοῖς κατὰ τὴν ἐρημίαν λῃσταῖς, οἳ πληγὰς ἐπέθηκαν, καὶ ἐξέδυσαν. Πρότερον πληγαὶ, καὶ τότε γύμνωσις. Πληγὴ ψυχῆς ἁμαρτία· γύμνωσις ψυχῆς ἀπόθεσις τοῦ ἐνδύματος τῆς ἀφθαρσίας. Ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀφανιστικὴ τῆς χάριτος τῆς δεδομένης ἡμῖν διὰ τοῦ λουτροῦ τῆς παλιγγενεσίας. Πορνεία, πληγὴ, μοιχεία, ἄλλη πληγὴ, πληγὴ ὁ φθόνος, πληγὴ ἕκαστον τούτων, πληγὴ αὐτὰ τὰ καίρια τύπτουσα, πληγὴ παρὰ λῃστῶν ἐμβαλλομένη, παρὰ δαιμόνων τῶν συνεργούντων ἡμῖν πρὸς τὰς ἁμαρτίας. Μετὰ τὰς πληγὰς ἐξεδύθη ὁ τετυμμένος. Εἰ σωματικὸν ἦν τὸ λεγόμενον, πρότερον ἐξέδυνον φειδοῖ τοῦ ἱματίου, καὶ τότε πληγὰς ἐπετίθεσαν. Ἢ ἐκδύσαντες ἂν, πληγὰς ἐπέθηκαν, ἵνα καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον διεσώθη, καὶ ὁ τυπτηθεὶς ἐπλήγη. Νῦν μέντοι πληγαὶ τῆς ἐκδύσεως προηγοῦνται, ἵνα μάθῃς, ὅτι ἁμαρτία προηγεῖται τῆς ἀποθέσεως τοῦ χαρίσματος, τοῦ δεδομένου σοι διὰ τῆς τοῦ Κυρίου φιλανθρωπίας. Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The devil fights God through the soul robbed and wounded by sin
orientation: The preacher is tracing envy to the devil and reading the man who fell among robbers as the soul wounded by sin.
pass_a_gloss: But the one that does not reason, because of its excessive impulse, as if he were a man, tears the paper, and there it shows its hatred of man. So also the devil showed in the image his hatred of God, because he was not able to lay hold of God. Thus the war against us has proof that the evil one is a fighter against God, and that he wars first against the Master. That one brought the man down from Jerusalem to Jericho, from the high places to the hollow places. Jerusalem is on the mountain land; but Jericho is down below by the salty sea. If any of you knows the place, he knows the truth of the things said, that Jericho holds the hollows of Palestine, but Jerusalem is fixed on the summit, holding the top of the mountain that stands up through all that country. From the high places to the low places then the man came, in order that he might fall in with robbers; having gone out of the safety that is at Jerusalem, in order that he might become easy to capture by the robbers in the deserted land, who laid on wounds and stripped him. First wounds, and then stripping. Sin is a wound of the soul; stripping of the soul is the laying aside of the garment of incorruption. And sin is destructive of the grace given to us through the washing of the new birth. Sexual immorality is a wound, adultery is another wound, envy is a wound, each of these is a wound, a wound striking the vital parts themselves, a wound put in by robbers, by demons who work together with us toward our sins. After the wounds the one who had been struck was stripped. If what is said were bodily, they would first strip him with sparing for the garment, and then they would lay on wounds. Or having stripped him, they would have laid on wounds, in order that both the garment might be kept safe and the one beaten might be wounded. But as it is wounds go before the stripping, in order that you may learn that sin goes before the laying aside of the gift, the gift given to you through the love for humankind of the Lord. To him be the glory to the ages of the ages. Amen.

bible_refs.note: ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἱεριχὼ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ... τοῖς λῃσταῖς περιπέσῃ ... πληγὰς ἐπέθηκαν, καὶ ἐξέδυσαν

pass_b_english: It does not stop to judge. Driven hard by its rush, it takes the paper for a man and tears it apart. There it shows its hatred for mankind. So too the devil showed his hatred of God in the image, for he could not lay hold of God. The war he wages against us proves the evil one fights against God, and he fights the Master first.

He is the one who brought the man down from Jerusalem to Jericho (Luke 10:30), from the high country to the low country. Jerusalem sits in the hill country. Jericho lies below, by the Salt Sea. If any of you know the land, you know these words are true. Jericho holds the low valleys of Palestine, while Jerusalem stands firm on the summit and holds the crown of the ridge that runs through the whole region. So the man came down from the heights to what lies below in order to fall among robbers. He left the safety of Jerusalem so that he might lie open to the robbers of the desert. They laid wounds upon him, and they stripped him.

Wounds come first, and then the stripping. Sin is a wound to the soul. The stripping of the soul is the casting off of the robe of incorruption. Sin wipes out the grace that was given to us through the washing of the new birth. Sexual sin is a wound, adultery is another wound, envy is a wound. Each of these is a wound, a wound that hits where life lives, a wound laid on by robbers, by demons who join us toward our sins. Only after the wounds was the wounded man stripped.

If this were a matter of the body, robbers would strip a man first to spare his clothing, and only then lay wounds on him. They would strip him first and then wound him, to save the garment and still wound the man who wears it. Here it is the other way. The wounds come before the stripping. Learn from this that sin comes first, and then comes the casting off of the gift, the gift given to you by the kindness of the Lord. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
notes: Ἱερου-σαλὴμ is split across a line break in the source; read as one word with no missing text.

problems.quote: and there he fell among robbers
problems.source_quote: ἦλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἵνα τοῖς λῃσταῖς περιπέσῃ
problems.why: Purpose is lost: he came down in order to fall among robbers, not merely and then fell.
problems.fix: So the man came down from the heights to what lies below in order to fall among robbers.
problems.ruling: ἵνα τοῖς λῃσταῖς περιπέσῃ is a purpose clause: he came down 'in order to fall among robbers'; 'and there he fell' reduces it to sequence.

problems.quote: and so he lay open to the robbers of the desert
problems.source_quote: τῆς ἀσφαλείας ἐξελθὼν τῆς κατὰ Ἱερουσαλήμ, ἵνα εὐάλωτος γένηται τοῖς κατὰ τὴν ἐρημίαν λῃσταῖς
problems.why: Leaving Jerusalem’s safety was so that he might become easy prey, not only a result.
problems.fix: He left the safety of Jerusalem so that he might lie open to the robbers of the desert.
problems.ruling: ἵνα εὐάλωτος γένηται is purpose ('that he might become easy prey'); 'and so he lay open' renders it as mere result, changing the stated intent.
